opportunities.title: Post-Grant Academic & Digital Humanities Web-App Staticization
target_users: University libraries and institutional repository managers
opportunities.strongest_alternative: The Endings Project (UVic) + Webrecorder/Browsertrix (WACZ) + Zenodo/Software Heritage (note: JASPER/PKP PN/CLOCKSS cover static journals, not interactive web apps)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Wren et al. (2017) showed 94% of highly cited scientific resources relocate successfully on their own versus 34% of uncited ones, compute-heavy servers cannot be purely staticized, and no direct WTP exists for a new staticization tool.
opportunities.falsifier: Attempt semi-automated staticization/WASM packaging on 20 randomly sampled open-source decaying academic/DH web apps within 48 hours; if fewer than 25% retain core functionality due to heavy backend/DB dependencies, reject broad staticization.

demand.basis: Peer-reviewed studies confirm widespread scholarly web-service decay (R05, R07, R08), but no direct behavioral evidence shows researchers or libraries demanding a new staticization tool.

international.basis: Evidence spans 375 international journals and Web of Science citations across NA, EU, and Asia with shared open-science standards.

innovation.basis: Distinct from JASPER/PKP PN (static journals); Endings requires upfront redesign and WACZ captures presentation rather than computation, leaving a plausible retrofit gap.

theme.basis: Anchored in retired academic web services and WebCite's 2023 shutdown, though framed more around scholarly workflows than one iconic dead product.

ai.basis: AI can assist dependency analysis and static/WASM conversion, but much of the pipeline is achievable with deterministic static analysis.

feasibility.basis: A scoped prototype converting a class of open-source academic web apps into static/WACZ bundles is achievable within 7 days using public repositories.

demo.basis: Clear before/after showing a broken legacy research web app running offline in-browser, though requiring brief scholarly context.

sustainability.basis: Institutional/grant funding models exist for libraries, but no verified spending or WTP for a new staticization product.

changes.reason: Decay is demonstrated quantitatively, but demand for a new staticization tool is not yet demonstrated behaviorally.
No direct evidence that target labs/libraries want a new tool (aligning with rubric anchor 3 and B-G-C10 / C-G-C23).
Grant/library budgets exist in general, but WTP for a new preservation tool is unverified.

opportunities.title: Post-Shutdown SaaS & Federated Export Semantic Rehydration
target_users: Product/design teams and SMEs migrating off discontinued SaaS under EU Data Act
Fediverse (Mastodon/ActivityPub) users and instance admins facing server shutdowns
Users of closing small/mid platforms (e.g., Cohost, Glitch) holding raw export dumps
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Data Transfer Project (DTI) + native competitor importers (Figma, Miro, Notion) + operator-provided exports/redirects (Glitch, Cohost)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Leading competitors build free importers for major shutting-down rivals, closing platforms like Cohost and Glitch already shipped basic exports/redirects, dying operators have no budget, and exports may strip internal relational IDs.
opportunities.falsifier: Inspect 3 real export archives (Mastodon Activity Streams 2.0, Cohost export, and a Glitch/SaaS export); if original exports strip foreign-key/thread references so that <50% of relational context is recoverable, reject the space.

demand.basis: EU Data Act (Sept 2025), Mastodon's documented post-import gap, and Cohost/Glitch/InVision shutdowns confirm the problem, but direct WTP for a generic rehydrator is unverified.

international.basis: EU Data Act applies extraterritorially to EU-serving providers, DTI operates globally from NA, and SaaS/Fediverse lock-in affects NA, EU, and Asia.

innovation.basis: DTI/DTP handles simplified canonical models and Mastodon cannot import exported posts, leaving a concrete post-export relational usability gap.

theme.basis: Meets the gate when anchored to exports from specifically discontinued platforms (e.g., Cohost Jan 2025, Glitch hosting July 2025, or InVision Dec 2024), but risks drifting into generic ETL.

ai.basis: Deterministic parsers suffice for documented export formats (Mastodon AS2, Glitch git); AI is only useful for undocumented long-tail SaaS schemas and lacks benchmark proof.

feasibility.basis: A working core slice operating on legal real-world export files (e.g., Mastodon Activity Streams 2.0 or public Cohost/Glitch exports) is achievable within 7 days.

demo.basis: Highly visual under-3-minute before/after: ingesting an unusable flat JSON/ZIP export and restoring an interactive, linked workspace exportable to open formats.

sustainability.basis: Plausible B2B compliance wedge tied to EU Data Act switching mandates (fee ban Jan 2027), but no verified commercial spending for a new tool yet; dying operators cannot pay (B-O2).

changes.reason: B-O2 (shutdown window of small/mid platforms) and A-O2 address the same platform-closure data continuity problem from pre- vs post-export angles.
Conventional deterministic parsers handle known export formats (Mastodon AS2, Cohost JSON, Glitch git) cleanly without AI; AI only helps on undocumented schemas.
Downgraded alongside ai_role because deterministic baseline is strong and AI lift is unbenchmarked.
No direct evidence of target users paying for a new generic rehydration tool; Glitch and Cohost shipped basic exports (R29).
EU Data Act B2B model is plausible but unverified by actual contracts (B-G-C10).

opportunities.title: Automated Environment Discovery & Configuration for Institutional Software Emulation
target_users: Museums and national archives operating emulation infrastructure (EaaSI/SPN members)
opportunities.strongest_alternative: EaaSI (Yale/SPN) with manual archivist configuration + Internet Archive Software Collection + PRONOM/DROID format identification
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: The institutional GLAM market is tiny and grant-dependent (Mellon/Sloan/IMLS), the Oct 2024 DMCA §1201 decision rejected remote research access to preserved games, and deterministic signature/matrix tooling covers most standard formats.
opportunities.falsifier: Benchmark automated manual/header parsing plus sandbox boot-testing on 15 public/shareware DOS/Win3.1/Mac68k titles; if automated boot success is <50% or does not outperform default DOSBox/IA presets, reject.

demand.basis: Primary Stanford BDPL/EaaSI case study confirms 2 full days of manual trial-and-error for a single 1985 title, but the addressable institutional buyer base is narrow.

international.basis: Verified across NA and EU via SPN, EaaSI, DPC, and IIPC networks; direct Asian emulation deployment evidence was not found.

innovation.basis: No existing tool automates end-to-end documentation parsing, emulator/OS matrix matching, and sandboxed boot verification for EaaSI workflows.

theme.basis: Directly brings verifiably obsolete operating systems and discontinued software back to life.

ai.basis: Deterministic header/signature detection (PRONOM/DROID) plus scripted sandbox probing cover most standard cases; AI is only useful for parsing messy scanned manuals.

feasibility.basis: Feasible for 1-2 open emulators (e.g., DOSBox/v86 in browser) within 7 days, but carries material licensing risk around proprietary legacy OS images/ROMs.

demo.basis: Compelling under-3-minute demo: drop a legacy disk image and scanned manual, watch the system infer requirements and boot the software live.

sustainability.basis: Grant-funded institutional model evidenced (Yale EaaSI $3.5M Mellon/Sloan), but no commercial WTP for an add-on tool.

changes.reason: Conventional PRONOM/DROID format detection + curated compatibility matrices + deterministic sandbox probing can handle most standard legacy binaries without AI.
Adjusted to reflect strong deterministic baseline and absence of benchmark measuring AI gain on manual parsing (C-G-C22).
Institutional grants exist for EaaSI, but funding for a separate configuration tool is unverified (B-G-C10).

opportunities.title: End-of-Life Sunset & Community Handover Governance for Live-Service Platforms
target_users: Open-source server preservation communities (e.g., Pretendo Network, City of Heroes Homecoming)
Indie and mid-size EU game/platform publishers facing upcoming EC EOL code of conduct
Independent community platform operators planning graceful shutdowns
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Post-shutdown clean-room reverse engineering by volunteers (Pretendo Network, Wiimmfi, Homecoming) or manual publisher offline patches
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Major publishers oppose EOL obligations due to third-party middleware IP and liability, and the European Commission directly confirmed on June 16, 2026 (IP/26/1369) it cannot propose mandatory legislation due to IP rights.
opportunities.falsifier: Sample 20 live-service games shut down 2024-2026 (B-O1 test) and interview 10 indie studios on adopting a free EC-aligned EOL handover kit; if >=8/10 refuse due to middleware IP/liability or <10% of large-community games have legal exits, the blocker is legal, not technical.

demand.basis: 1,294,188 validated ECI signatures (R01, R28), 170 Pretendo repos (R13), and Homecoming player funding (B-R10) prove strong civic/community demand, but not direct demand for a new paid tool.

international.basis: Direct primary evidence across EU (ECI), NA (Cohost, Homecoming, DMCA §1201), and Asia (Nintendo 3DS/Wii U, Japanese gacha churn, Tianya Club).

innovation.basis: A standardized lightweight EOL handover kit is missing, but the core bottleneck is legal and economic rather than purely technical.

theme.basis: Directly anchored in discontinued online services (Nintendo Network 3DS/Wii U, City of Heroes, Cohost) and keeping them operational.

ai.basis: AI is unnecessary for the core problem of IP licensing, architecture decoupling, and EOL governance.

feasibility.basis: Depends on publisher cooperation not in hand or enters high-risk DRM/EULA reverse-engineering territory if built third-party.

demo.basis: Demonstrating a synthetic client-server sunset handover works technically but relies on synthetic apps rather than real commercial services.

sustainability.basis: High legal risk (EC IP/26/1369 confirms IP blocks legislation; DMCA §1201) and no verified payer after publisher support ends.

changes.reason: Independent convergence across all three agents on live-service/online game EOL and community revival.
ECI signatures prove civic/policy demand, not willingness to buy or adopt a new software tool (C-G-C19 and B-O1).

opportunities.title: Consent-Aware & Sovereign Community Digital Heritage Preservation
target_users: Indigenous and minority cultural heritage stewards (GIDA/CARE-aligned)
Independent community archives preserving shutting-down regional platforms
National libraries operating permission-based private web archiving (e.g., NDL WARP)
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Mukurtu CMS (v4 cultural protocols & migration) + Local Contexts Labels + PARADISEC offline static HTML/RO-Crates + NDL WARP
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Fails the Resurrection theme gate (<3) with no specific dead technology; Mukurtu + Local Contexts + PARADISEC already cover core cultural-protocol and offline heritage needs (R34, C-R19, C-R21); opt-in consent fails at web scale.
opportunities.falsifier: Withdrawn as a standalone Kiroween opportunity space; retain GDPR Art. 89, NDL Law, and CARE principles as cross-cutting legal/ethical constraints.

demand.basis: Strong legal and institutional signals, but no direct evidence of demand for a new tool over Mukurtu/Local Contexts/PARADISEC.

international.basis: Direct primary evidence across Japan (NDL WARP), Korea/Singapore (OASIS/IIPC), EU (GDPR Art. 89), NA (Hachette v. IA), and global Indigenous networks (GIDA).

innovation.basis: Direct verification of Mukurtu 4 migration (R34) plus Agent C's evidence on Local Contexts and PARADISEC offline collections (2026) shrinks the remaining gap.

theme.basis: Fails Resurrection gate (<3): focuses on archival ethics and legal compliance broadly rather than reviving a specific dead technology.

ai.basis: AI helps detect multilingual PII for GDPR Art. 89 review, replaceable partly by rules/NER and unbenchmarked.

feasibility.basis: A consent-tagged WACZ packaging and PII redaction pipeline is feasible within 7 days using open datasets.

demo.basis: Policy- and compliance-oriented value requires domain explanation.

sustainability.basis: Grant-dependent institutional/NGO model with no verified commercial WTP.

changes.reason: Fails Resurrection theme gate (<3) as confirmed independently by C-O3 (theme: 1), and existing specialized tools (Mukurtu 4, Local Contexts, PARADISEC offline HTML) already cover core workflows.
Direct inspection of Mukurtu migration docs (R34) and Agent C's PARADISEC 2026 evidence narrows the novelty gap.
